one_liner: Pure-Rust, bit-exact port of fixed-point libopus 1.5.2; runs at about parity with the C reference, not faster.
what_it_does: ropus reimplements the Opus codec (SILK, CELT, hybrid, multistream, projection/ambisonics, repacketizer, FEC, DTX, plus LPCNet/FARGAN PLC and DRED encode) in Rust, so a build needs no C toolchain. The crate has a typed high-level API (Encoder::builder, Decoder::decode with DecodeMode) and a low-level layer that mirrors the libopus C API; an unpublished capi/ crate exposes the libopus C ABI, and xiph's seven test programs compile against it unmodified. Output is meant to be bit-exact with libopus built in fixed-point mode, and a differential FFI harness checks this.
how_it_is_fast: It is a line-by-line port of libopus's fixed-point code, not a new algorithm; speed comes from compiler work. Hot kernels use the wide crate's portable SIMD types plus unchecked indexing in the SILK and CELT inner loops (NSQ, Burg, autocorrelation, FFT butterflies, MDCT rotations), and the workspace builds with ThinLTO, codegen-units = 1 and target-cpu x86-64-v3 (apple-a14 on macOS ARM), so LLVM auto-vectorises at 256-bit width. There are no hand-written intrinsics; the project's April journal credits the x86-64-v3 switch alone with moving mean encode from 1.19x to 1.02x of C.
when_to_use: Rust projects (native or WebAssembly) that want Opus without linking C libopus or needing a C compiler; videocall.rs reports using it in production for encode and NetEQ decode, including WASM clients (issue #1).

When output must match fixed-point libopus 1.5.2 byte for byte (decode, and encode outside the tonality-analysis path), for example to test against a C reference or to replace audiopus or opus-sys bindings without changing bitstreams.
When you need features most other ports skip: multistream, ambisonics projection, the repacketizer, in-band FEC/DTX and neural PLC.
Throughput similar to the C reference is enough: about 1.06x encode and 1.01x decode time on x86-64 with the workspace's x86-64-v3 build.
when_not_to_use: If the goal is more speed than libopus: it is at parity on x86-64 and 16-22% slower on Apple M1 Pro, and several sibling ports report real speed-ups.

Default crates.io builds on x86-64: the x86-64-v3 flag lives in the workspace's .cargo/config.toml, which dependents do not inherit, so a plain cargo add build targets baseline x86-64; the project's own generic-target run was about 1.19x slower than C on encode (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, before the bench fix).
When you need bit-exactness with the float libopus that distributions ship: ropus tracks the fixed-point build, so decoded PCM will not match a float build bit for bit.
When you need DRED PCM reconstruction (opus_decoder_dred_decode*), OSCE, QEXT or custom modes: these are deferred or not ported.

When maturity and outside review matter: one maintainer with AI agents doing most of the work (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, codex and claude co-authored commits); 9 stars; the latest crates.io release, 0.12.18 (2026-05-11), is four months behind the repository.

integration.dependencies: wide 0.7 (runtime); cc (build script, only used when xiph reference sources are on disk)
integration.platforms: Any Rust target via portable code; tuned for x86-64-v3 (AVX2, FMA, BMI2) and Apple M1 (apple-a14) in workspace builds; WebAssembly reported by a downstream user; no hand-written intrinsics on any platform
integration.thread_safety: Encoder and Decoder are Send and Sync (checked by a compile-time test); encode and decode take &mut self, so use one instance per thread or guard it with a Mutex.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the low-level Rust API mirrors libopus, and the repository's capi/ crate (publish = false, built as the mdopus_capi staticlib) exposes the libopus C ABI and passes xiph's test programs, but it is not published, it does not expose the DRED decode calls, and its output matches the fixed-point libopus build, not the usual float build.

gotchas: The crates.io package ships an empty DNN weights blob (build.rs only embeds weights when the xiph reference tree is on disk), so neural PLC and DRED fall back to classical PLC unless you call set_dnn_blob; workspace builds instead embed an 8.78 MB blob that takes about 3.34 ms to load per decoder.

Published numbers come from a harness with since-fixed measurement flaws. At commit 54fef85 (x86 table, 2026-05-11) and at the 2026-07-31 Apple run, harness/Cargo.toml always enabled trace-silk-encode, so Rust SILK encode pushed trace records into an unbounded Mutex<Vec>, while C ran a harness-modified traced enc_API.c (project bug ROP-BUG-FLUX-00026, severity High). The C timer also included one codec create and destroy per run (ROP-BUG-FLUX-00027). Both were fixed on 2026-08-01, but the README tables were not re-measured, and the size of either effect is unmeasured.

The C baseline is the harness's own build: fixed-point, -msse4.1 applied to every C file, SSE4.1-only runtime dispatch (libopus 1.5.2's AVX2 NSQ_del_dec source is not compiled) and -ffp-contract=off. The Rust side gets x86-64-v3, so the 'C dispatches to hand-tuned SSE4.1/AVX2' wording overstates the baseline.

The crates.io README still shows the stale April table (encode 1.02x, decode 0.95x, Ryzen 9 9950X3D), measured before the bench fix that took decoder construction and its weight load out of the timed loop.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ropus over the faster Opus ports (opuspp, opus-pure, ruopus, rusty-opus, gopus) when you need a full libopus API surface (multistream, projection, repacketizer, PLC) and bit-exact agreement with fixed-point libopus 1.5.2, checked by a differential harness and the RFC 6716/8251 vectors, rather than extra speed. For lower CPU cost, those siblings, or libopus-rs's 1-5% gain, are better candidates.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own tools/bench_sweep.sh (harness cmd_bench, 10 WAV vectors, CBR, complexity 10, 20 ms frames, C encode and decode timed before Rust in a fixed order, no output comparison) on an i7-14700KF under WSL2 gives Rust/C time ratios with a mean of 1.06x for encode and 1.01x for decode (medians of 5 sweeps; the sub-1.0 rows fall inside the 0.02-0.32 cross-sweep spread). On Apple M1 Pro against upstream NEON C the means are 1.16x and 1.22x. The baseline is the harness's fixed-point, SSE4.1-only libopus 1.5.2, compiler versions are unstated, and both tables predate the 2026-08-01 harness fixes.
status_note: Very active (1,289 commits, last 2026-09-13; the 99 of 124 internal bug-ledger records fetched are all Closed) and BSD-3-Clause, so it can be copied freely, but it is a young, mostly AI-written port whose crates.io release lags the repository and which is no faster than the C library it replaces.
